description:
## Goal

A normal `git push` must run a tracked, documented verification gate that covers every target CI tests, so integration-target or coverage-environment failures do not first appear after the push.

## Current state

Verified at origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`:

- `.githooks/` contains only executable `pre-commit`; there is no `pre-push`.
- The effective `core.hooksPath` points at `/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz/.githooks`, which also contains only `pre-commit`.
- `pre-commit` runs conditional `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo check --all`, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- CI lint runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the same workspace clippy command. The old missing-`--workspace` clippy defect is fixed.
- CI test runs `cargo audit`, `cargo test --workspace --doc`, and `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --workspace` with the repository coverage threshold.
- The workspace has three integration-test targets: `aot_variadic_open`, `fixture_matrix`, and `fz2_cli`.
- README documents `cargo test --workspace` as the whole suite, but that is not CI parity: it omits audit and the all-features coverage run. Coverage-sensitive gate documentation is owned by fz-f98.25.

The pre-commit header's "Mirrors the CI lint job" wording is also imprecise: the hook adds `cargo check`, and its formatting behavior modifies/re-stages staged Rust rather than running CI's check-only command.

## Strategy

Define one tracked push-gate entry point rather than copying a command list into another hook. Add an executable `.githooks/pre-push` that invokes it.

Make the shared gate cover every CI-tested Rust target, including the all-features coverage environment and threshold. Reuse the same tracked command surface from CI where practical so target selection cannot drift independently. Keep CI-only artifact upload and environment/tool installation in the workflow.

Coordinate contributor-facing prerequisite and gate documentation with fz-f98.25; do not duplicate that ticket's coverage-predicate production/test cleanup.

Update the pre-commit header to describe its actual narrower commit-time role. Do not claim that it is the complete CI or push gate.

## Checks

- `.githooks/pre-push` exists, is executable, and delegates to the tracked gate.
- A normal push is rejected when any of `aot_variadic_open`, `fixture_matrix`, or `fz2_cli` fails.
- The gate exercises the coverage-sensitive path with all features and enforces `.coverage-threshold`.
- Workspace doctests and the dependency audit remain represented in the documented CI/push contract, with required local tools stated explicitly.
- CI and pre-push share target-selection commands rather than maintaining independent lists.
- The pre-commit header accurately describes formatting, compile-check, and workspace-clippy behavior.
- Add shell-level regression coverage that proves command ordering, failure propagation, and argument forwarding without running the full suite.
title: Add an explicit pre-push gate for every CI-tested target
